status.headline: Mods open when GTA VI comes to PC
status.text: GTA VI launches on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S on November 19, 2026. Rockstar hasn't announced a PC version, and consoles don't run mods, so there's nothing to upload yet. We're building the hub, the rules and the developer guides now, so creators are ready on day one.
status.pcEstimate: If Rockstar follows its own pattern, a PC version would land somewhere between late 2027 and 2028. That's our estimate, not an announcement.

rockstarRules.source: Rockstar Games modding guidelines, as reported by Game Developer and GamesRadar
rules: Don't expand or change Rockstar's official storylines, missions, characters or continuity.
Don't bring maps, locations, characters or assets from one Rockstar game into another.
Don't port games to platforms Rockstar hasn't released them on.
Multiplayer modding goes through Rockstar's licensed Creator Platform (FiveM/RedM), unless Rockstar says otherwise.
No real brands, logos, car makes, music, artwork or other games' content, and no Rockstar voice performances reused.
No real person's voice, image or likeness without written permission.
Paid mods through approved stores only
Mods can only be sold through storefronts Rockstar approves, such as its Cfx Marketplace. Everywhere else, modding has to be non-commercial.
No gambling, loot boxes or crypto
No real-money gambling, loot boxes, sale of in-game currency, or crypto, NFTs or memecoins.

standards: Every upload must follow Rockstar's modding guidelines and our rules. Anything that breaks them is rejected, however good it is.
Original work, or work you have written permission to use, with every contributor credited. No ripped or stolen assets.
Nothing that works online, gives an unfair advantage or touches GTA Online.
At least three unedited in-game screenshots, a clear description, install and uninstall steps, requirements and a version number.
Tested on the current game version, with no crashes, no broken saves and no major performance hit.
Every file is virus-scanned. Script mods need readable code or pass a manual code review; no obfuscated installers or bundled adware.
Content that looks like it belongs in Leonida: fictional brands, original designs, Rockstar's tone.
A changelog for every update, and a fix or a takedown when a game update breaks it.
review: Upload your files, screenshots and description from your creator account.
Virus scan, file-type and size checks, and a duplicate check against existing uploads.
A moderator installs and tests the mod against the rules and the quality bar.
Approved mods go live with your name on them. Great work gets a Staff Pick.
tiers: Anyone with a verified account who has had a mod approved.
Three or more approved mods with no rule breaks. Faster reviews and a badge.
Manually approved creators with a track record who can list paid mods. Application only.
Creators who join before the PC launch. A permanent badge and early access to uploads.

guide.title: Will GTA 6 have mods?
guide.summary: Where GTA VI modding stands today: consoles, PC, Rockstar's rules and FiveM.
sections: PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S don't let you load custom game files, and Rockstar has never supported mods on console. Expect GTA VI on console to stay unmodded.
Every modern GTA reached PC after console, and each PC release grew a huge modding scene. Rockstar hasn't announced a PC version of GTA VI yet.

Rockstar has long said it generally won't act against single-player PC mods that are non-commercial and respect other people's IP. In September 2026 it published stricter guidelines that also cover GTA VI.

Rockstar bought Cfx.re, the team behind FiveM and RedM, in August 2023, and opened an official storefront for FiveM and RedM creators in January 2026. A FiveM-style platform for GTA VI is plausible but unannounced.
Single-player PC modding will almost certainly happen once a PC version ships. Multiplayer and roleplay modding will likely be channelled through Rockstar's own platform.

guide.title: Engine and technical specs
guide.summary: What we know and what we expect about the engine GTA VI runs on.
sections: GTA VI runs on Rockstar's own engine, the Rockstar Advanced Game Engine (RAGE), which powered GTA IV, GTA V and Red Dead Redemption 2. Fans often call this version "RAGE 9"; Rockstar hasn't used that name.
On PC, expect DirectX 12. GTA V's 2025 Enhanced edition and Red Dead Redemption 2 both use it, and RDR2 also supports Vulkan.
GTA V Enhanced added ray-traced shadows, reflections and global illumination. A PC GTA VI will almost certainly build on that.
Leonida is far denser than Los Santos, so assets stream in and out constantly. Mods that add a lot of map content will need to respect streaming budgets more than in GTA V.
Rockstar uses Euphoria for character physics and its own systems for vehicles. The Extended Look's weightier driving suggests a reworked vehicle model, which means handling mods will need new tuning.

guide.title: Scripting and programming languages
guide.summary: How script mods worked in GTA V, and the languages to learn for GTA VI.
sections: Rockstar's scripts drive the game by calling thousands of engine functions called natives (spawn a car, set a wanted level, play an animation). Script hooks let mods call the same natives.
Script Hook V let C++ mods (.asi plugins) call natives directly. It appeared within days of GTA V's PC launch. Expect the same pattern for GTA VI: learn modern C++.
Script Hook V .NET and RAGE Plugin Hook brought C# to GTA V; LSPDFR is built on RAGE Plugin Hook. C# is the friendliest route for gameplay mods.
FiveM servers run Lua and JavaScript. If Rockstar's platform supports GTA VI, those skills transfer directly.
Graphics mods and ReShade presets use HLSL-style shader code.
C# for gameplay scripts, C++ for low-level tools, Lua for roleplay, and Python for asset pipelines and converters.

guide.title: Game folder structure
guide.summary: How a GTA V install is laid out, and how GTA VI's will probably look.
tree: │  └─ x64/dlcpacks/          each DLC as its own dlc.rpf
├─ mods/                     OpenIV's mod copy of edited archives
├─ plugins/                  RAGE Plugin Hook and LSPDFR
sections: OpenIV's "mods" folder kept the original archives untouched so updates didn't break installs. A GTA VI hub should push the same safe approach.
Rockstar adds content as separate DLC packs; add-on mods copied that structure so they didn't overwrite base files.
Expect a similar layout: an executable, core archives, an update archive and per-update packs. Folder names will differ.

guide.title: Rockstar's modding rules
guide.summary: Rockstar's September 2026 modding guidelines in plain English, and what they mean for you.
sections: Single-player PC mods that are free, original, lore-friendly and don't touch online play: scripts, graphics, interiors, original vehicles and outfits, police mods.
Allowed only through storefronts Rockstar approves. GTA6 Project lists paid mods from verified sellers and sends buyers to the approved store to pay.
Real-world cars and brands were a huge part of GTA V modding. Under the new guidelines they count as other people's IP, so we won't host them.
Story or character edits, ports from other Rockstar games, online cheats, selling mods outside Rockstar-approved stores, gambling and crypto.
This is our reading of public guidelines. Rockstar's own wording always wins.

selling.intro: Most mods on GTA6 Project are free. A small group of verified sellers, approved by hand, can also list premium mods. Buyers always pay through a storefront Rockstar has approved, so creators get paid and stay inside Rockstar's rules.
how: Have at least five approved free mods on GTA6 Project, six months of history and a clean record: no rule breaks, no stolen assets, no unresolved reports.
Send your profile, your best work and what you plan to sell. We look at quality, support history and how you treat users.
A staff member reviews every application by hand. There's no automatic route and no paying to skip the queue.
Set up on an approved store
Sell through a storefront Rockstar has approved, such as the Cfx Marketplace once it covers GTA VI. We check your store listing matches your upload.
Your premium mod gets a full page here, with screenshots, reviews, the price and a buy button that goes to your approved store listing.
requirements: Every sale goes through a storefront Rockstar has approved. No PayPal links, Patreon paywalls, Discord sales or direct bank transfers.
Everything in a paid mod must be yours or licensed for commercial use. No Rockstar assets, missions or DLC behind a paywall, and no real brands.
Paid mods sit beside free work, not instead of it. Sellers keep publishing free mods too.
No loot boxes, gacha, random rewards for money, in-game currency sales, crypto or NFTs.
Real in-game screenshots, clear features, the game version it works on, and a refund policy that follows UK and EU consumer law.
Paying users get fixes when a game update breaks the mod. Abandoned paid mods are delisted.
Paid mods go through the full human review and virus scan, and can be pulled at any time if they break the rules.
selling.lose: Selling status is removed for stolen or ripped content, selling outside approved stores, misleading listings, ignoring refunds or support, or any breach of Rockstar's guidelines.
selling.future: If Rockstar approves GTA6 Project as a storefront, verified sellers will be able to sell directly on the site. Until then, every purchase happens on an approved store.
selling.apply: Selling opens after GTA VI reaches PC and uploads go live. Founding creators can register interest now.
